title: Relative clauses and reported speech
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Relative clauses with prepositions
lessons.explanation: A relative clause that needs a preposition keeps the preposition in front of the relative word: a casa em que moro, o livro de que preciso, o homem com quem falei, a empresa para a qual trabalho. After a preposition, use que for things, quem for people, or o qual, a qual, os quais and as quais, which agree with the noun and fuse with the preposition: pelo qual, pela qual, nos quais. Without the preposition the relative is wrong in standard writing: a casa que moro is wrong. A clause that adds extra information about a unique noun sits between commas (Maria, que mora aqui, é médica); a restrictive clause that identifies the noun has none.

examples.en: The house I live in is old.

lessons.title: Cujo and onde, aonde, donde
lessons.explanation: Cujo means whose and agrees with the thing possessed, not with the owner: o autor cujo livro li, a mulher cuja filha estuda aqui, os alunos cujas notas são altas. It is never followed by an article. Onde marks a place where something is (o hotel onde ficamos), aonde marks movement toward a place, a + onde (a cidade aonde vamos), and donde marks movement from a place, de + onde (a cidade donde viemos). Do not use que with a possessive for whose (o autor que o livro li is wrong), and do not use onde for movement toward or away from a place in careful writing.

lessons.title: Reported statements: tense and time shifts
lessons.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past, the reported verb usually moves back one step: presente becomes imperfeito (estou becomes estava), pretérito perfeito becomes mais-que-perfeito (cheguei becomes tinha chegado), futuro becomes futuro do pretérito (viajarei becomes viajaria). Pronouns and time words shift too: hoje becomes naquele dia, ontem becomes no dia anterior, amanhã becomes no dia seguinte, aqui becomes ali or lá. Use que to introduce the report. The shift is the norm in writing; if the situation is still true, speakers may keep the present, but the shifted form is the correct test in this course. Do not leave a present or future verb after a past reporting verb when the shift applies.

lessons.title: Reported questions and requests
lessons.explanation: A reported yes/no question uses se: ela perguntou se eu estava cansado. A reported question with a question word keeps that word and moves the verb back: ele perguntou onde eu morava, ela perguntou o que eu queria. A reported request or order uses que plus the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb: ele pediu que eu esperasse, o chefe mandou que nós saíssemos, a professora pediu que os alunos prestassem atenção. Do not use que for a yes/no question (perguntou que eu estava is wrong) and do not leave the present indicative or the infinitive after que in a request.

examples.en: She asked whether I was tired.

lessons.title: Reporting verbs that mark stance
lessons.explanation: The reporting verb shows how the speaker treats a claim. Alegar reports a claim without vouching for it (ele alegou que estava doente). Afirmar, garantir and admitir report what the person stated, promised or conceded, with the indicative and the shifted tense (ela admitiu que errou, o diretor garantiu que a obra estaria pronta). Negar que and sugerir que take the subjunctive after a past verb: ele negou que tivesse mentido, ela sugeriu que esperássemos. Negar may also take an infinitive (negou ter mentido). Do not use the indicative after negar que or sugerir que, and do not use the subjunctive after alegar que or admitir que.

examples.en: He denied that he had lied.
